E1-01.why: guess — four bare placement labels (Point A/D/C/B) in scrambled order; nothing in the option set discriminates without the passage

E1-02.why: guess — tense/agreement bracket (let / had let / lets / No Change) names the axis but does not resolve it; picked the simple past-or-plural form as the least marked member

E1-03.why: elimination-to-the-residue on No Change — the two propositions are contrastive (not a performer, yet will be in front of thousands), so 'so' and 'because' both assert a causation that runs the wrong way and 'and' flattens the contrast; the unseen original almost certainly carries but/yet

E1-04.why: guess — placement labels only, no discriminating content

E1-05.why: register sandwich — B is colloquial ('bothered to even glance at the thing'), C is inflated passive ('never once been forthcoming'), D is padded ('not one soul', 'fifteen long years'); one idea at three registers leaves the unseen plain original as the key

E1-06.why: punctuation singleton — semicolons in A are unlicensed with no internal commas, C drops the coordinating conjunction, so only B is the standard three-item series; No Change is presumed to carry the tested error

E1-07.why: elimination-to-the-residue on No Change — B strips the commas from a nonrestrictive relative, C shifts to present 'sells' against the past 'wanted', D is a number singleton ('their' for a singular owner); all three alternates fail independently

E1-08.why: near-guess — Yes/No purpose item with a balanced 2 Yes / 2 No split and matched lengths on the two serious options; chose C because its reason is self-certifying (returns to inexperience, closes by naming it the point) where B's asserts an absence; A and D are throwaways whose reasons would not support their polarity

E1-09.why: dialogue-tag bracket — A ends the quote with a period and capitalises a fragment ('He explains.'), C imposes a question mark on an explanation, so only the comma-before-lowercase-tag form survives

E1-10.why: guess — the four options are a clean 2x2 over comma/no-comma and stay/stayed, which names both axes but resolves neither; picked no-comma (a comma would split subject from verb) plus the present for a general statement about tides
